requirements_summary:
Primary concern is p95 tail latency for interactive traffic when co-scheduled with long prompts.

Workload mix (as described):
- Interactive support agent chat: short prompts, streaming, latency-sensitive.
- Doc summarization / investigation workflows: long contexts (10k–32k tokens), prefill-heavy, throughput-oriented, may run continuously (not just nightly).
- Some retrieval/doc-search components (embeddings + rerank) mentioned, but the buying decision is driven by text generation tails.

Latency/SLO targets (customer-stated, for interactive/chat):
- p95 end-to-end <250–350ms for short requests on their typical context sizes (excluding network; they will measure from their VPC).
- p99 must be "boring" (their words): they have timeouts today during long-prompt batch windows.
- Wants explicit plan for overload behavior (admission control / backpressure) rather than queue buildup.

Throughput/cost:
- Will accept small throughput loss if tails improve and isolation is real; they gave an explicit bound of <=5% throughput regression for the mixed-workload policy vs baseline in our test.
- Cost sensitivity is moderate; stability and predictability beats raw $/1M tokens right now.

Model + platform requirements:
- Needs streaming, tool/function calling, structured outputs.
- Needs version pinning + rollback (they are cautious about silent behavior changes).
- Wants dedicated capacity (noisy-neighbor concerns); prefers VPC deployment for compliance.

Security/compliance:
- SSO/SAML required for console.
- Audit logs + retention controls (customer asked for configurable retention / export to their SIEM).
- KMS integration preferred; data residency in US regions.

Open questions from HelioPay:
- "How do you prove p95 stays stable when long prompts hit the system?" (asked multiple times)
- Whether scheduler prototype is per-route / per-deployment configurable and how it interacts with customer tiering.
- What the rollback trigger looks like in practice (dashboards + thresholds).
notes:
Account summary (HelioPay): enterprise payments company evaluating Redwood to replace a mix of managed API + in-house GPU inference.

Key pain:
- Their current setup has "batch windows" where long-context jobs cause interactive chat p95 to spike; they described it as noisy-neighbor even when they think they have enough GPU headroom.
- They want Dedicated or Private-in-VPC specifically to control isolation, but still need evidence that scheduling avoids tail blow-ups.

What resonated:
- Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (short/long prompt-aware queues) + explicit starvation bounds.
- Instrumentation: per-class queue depth/wait time + prefill vs decode split; they asked to see these on canary dashboards.

Customer asks / deliverables requested:
- Benchmark proof using a mixed prompt-length distribution that mirrors them (short chat + long summarization concurrently). They want p50/p95/p99 and throughput/GPU util deltas.
- Explanation of failure modes (misclassification, long-prompt starvation, oscillations under burst) and what guardrails exist.
- Clear rollback criteria and whether feature is default-off (they prefer default-off and opt-in per route).

- Omar (SE) coordinating with Jonas/Rina for trace-based replay runs; Sofia team can provide policy knobs + recommended defaults.
